Dates below are ePrint received / last-revised dates. novelty_vs_programme checked against brief/FRONTIER_KNOWN_RESULTS_IC.txt (28 rows) and brief/LEAD_ATLAS_DISPOSITIONS.tsv (154 leads).

papers.title: Bounds on polynomial approximations of the discrete logarithm function
papers.authors: Swastik Kopparty, Rishabh Kothary, Ashutosh Shankar
papers.summary: Revisits Coppersmith-Shparlinski (2000): a univariate f in F_p[X] of degree <= D agrees with dlog(x) on at most sqrt(2Dp) points. New: (1+o(1))sqrt(Dp) for all D via list-decoding (matches the Johnson bound, nontrivial even for D > p/2); for D=1 the bound drops to O(p^{2/5}) via sum-product estimates from additive combinatorics; bivariate Q(X,Y) vanishing on (x, dlog x) also improved toward the Johnson analogue.
papers.relevance: Directly about the programme's 'no low-degree membership / only algebraic handle over F_p is x as an integer' wall (brief section 2) and the x-functional-filter lever (KN-OPEN-91d4f6): it quantifies how badly any low-degree polynomial in the field representation can correlate with a dlog, which is exactly the obstruction a non-generic prime-field oracle must evade. The Johnson-bound/list-decoding framing and the additive-combinatorics route are new lenses; the paper is about F_p^*, not E(F_p). The elliptic analogue (polynomial in x(P) agreeing with log_G(P)) is not stated and is the natural question.
papers.suggested_route: Theory+toy: (a) state and test the elliptic analogue at p ~ 10^3..10^4 (prime-order E, compute max agreement of degree-D polynomials in x(P) with log_G(P) via Guruswami-Sudan style list decoding on the point set {(x(P), log P)}; compare to sqrt(Dp)); (b) check whether the bivariate bound kills 'x-functional filters' outright by bounding correlation between any degree-D functional of x-coordinates and sums (the filter must be a polynomial in coordinates agreeing with a group-law relation on many points). Falsifier: if elliptic agreement matches the Johnson bound at toy scale, filters of degree D cannot gain more than sqrt(D/p) per bucket, closing KN-OPEN-91d4f6 for polynomial filters.

papers.title: Hamming Ideals and Grobner Bases for ISD-like Syndrome Decoding
papers.authors: Roberto La Scala, Marco Marchesin, Sharwan K. Tiwari
papers.summary: Derives the defining equations of the Hamming variety (vectors of weight <= w) in terms of elementary symmetric functions; because these have high degree, uses convolution identities for elementary symmetric functions and Lucas'-identity factorizations to obtain an equivalent presentation with auxiliary variables and equations of bounded degree. Combines with an ISD-like strategy (fix only part of an information set) and a MultiSolve hybrid (many Groebner computations on specialized systems). Experiments on Classic McEliece Category-1-sized random binary SDP instances.
papers.relevance: Lever 6 of the brief: non-subspace Frobenius-stable bases at prime n, where the Hamming-ball base has 'a bounded-degree Hamming-ideal membership (KN-OPEN-5e3dd0)'. This paper gives an explicit bounded-degree presentation of exactly that ideal over F_2 with auxiliary variables, i.e. a ready-made membership system to append to a Weil-descended S_{m+1}. Unknown: how the auxiliary variables change first/last fall degree of the combined system.
papers.suggested_route: Toy experiment (msolve over F_2): descend S_3 over F_{2^n}, n=13..33, with factor base B(n,w) (Hamming ball, Frobenius-stable at prime n when using a normal basis), impose membership via the bounded-degree Hamming-ideal presentation of this paper; measure d_ff, d_F/solving degree and decomposition yield vs a linear-subspace base of equal size. Falsifier: solving degree >= subspace-base solving degree at equal |B| (then the Hamming ball buys only Frobenius-stability, a /n factor, i.e. constant/engineering).

papers.title: Derivative-Based Evaluation of Multivariate Polynomials over Product Hamming Balls
papers.authors: Vaibhav Dixit, Santanu Sarkar, Fukang Liu, Willi Meier
papers.date: received 2026-02-06, last revised 2026-09-29 (3rd revision; in window by revision only)
papers.summary: Unified derivative-based framework (initialization + evaluation phases) for evaluating a degree-d multivariate polynomial on all points of a product Hamming ball B(n,w) = B(n_s,w_s) x ... x B(n_1,w_1), first over F_q then over F_{q^rho} by basis expansion. Initialization O(nrM) or O(rM^2) with M <= min(C(n+d,d), q^n), r = min(d, q-1); afterwards evaluation costs O(d |B|) operations with memory independent of the number of evaluated points.
papers.relevance: An enumeration oracle for a Hamming-ball factor base: evaluating a descended summation polynomial on every base element costs O(d) per point. Because it is pure enumeration, the generic-oracle bound (S T^2 >= r/|Aut|) applies; it is an engineering/constant-factor device for measuring Hamming-ball decomposition yield cheaply, not an advance.
papers.suggested_route: Use as the cheap census tool for the Hamming-ball experiments of 2026/2062 (yield and variance of decompositions over B(n,w) at n=13..25). Classify as engineering. No falsifier beyond matching the generic bound.

papers.title: Smoothing the degree of regularity for polynomial systems
papers.authors: Samuel Jaques, Lars Ran, Simona Samardjiska, Melvin Seitner
papers.date: received 2026-02-27, last revised 2026-10-07 (in window by revision; ASIACRYPT 2026)
papers.summary: Argues the integer degree of regularity is a coarse cost parameter for XL/F4/F5 and defines a 'smoothed' (fractional) degree by working with specific Macaulay submatrices between two consecutive degrees that still suffice to solve. Under an assumption generalizing semi-regularity (checked experimentally) this smooths XL complexity for MQ; applied to a recent UOV attack it saves a few bits.
papers.relevance: Lever 1 and 4 of the brief (growth of solving degree of descended S_{m+1}; the PKM-tower plateau D = 6,6,7,7 at N=9..18 that contradicts the naive XL bound). A fractional degree-of-regularity measurement could explain a plateau that integer D cannot, and sharpens the (m, l) grid measurements. FRONTIER row 'Modern Groebner-basis complexity refinements' is known_bound but does not include this smoothing.
papers.suggested_route: Re-measure the PKM tower t=1..14 and binary descended S_3 at n=13..25 with smoothed-degree Macaulay submatrices (own XL over F_2 or msolve traces): record fractional d_reg next to integer D and the closure certificate. Prediction to test: d_F = 4 + floor((t-2)/4). Falsifier: fractional d_reg tracks integer D exactly (no information gained).

papers.title: A Memory-efficient Implementation of Wiedemann XL
papers.authors: Daniel Cabarcas, Tung Chou, Felipe Merino, Javier Verbel
papers.summary: First efficient on-the-fly implementation of XL with block Wiedemann: Macaulay rows generated on the fly in BW1 without column-index tables, new O(n^2) column-index algorithm (vs O(n^3) lookups); builds on Cheng-Chou-Niederhagen-Yang (F_2, F_16, F_31, SSE) and ports to AVX2 over F_256. Running times comparable to CCNY with up to 5x less memory.
papers.relevance: Enabler for the decisive unmeasured cells (m,l)=(4,4),(4,5),(4,6) and larger n in the descended S_5 grid, where memory of the Macaulay matrix is the binding constraint; alternative to lever 5 (Frobenius-equivariant F4). Engineering only; cannot change an exponent.
papers.suggested_route: Engineering: run on-the-fly XL-BW over F_2 on descended S_5 systems for the (4,4),(4,5),(4,6) cells at the largest n that fits in memory; record solving degree. Classify as engineering.

papers.title: Attacking UOV-based Signatures with Schur--Macaulay Matrices
papers.authors: Simon-Philipp Merz, Lars Ran
papers.summary: Two new equation-generation mechanisms for systems of quadratic forms in characteristic 2: (1) 'divided squares': over Z, omega wedge omega = 2 omega^{(2)}, so in char 2 the square vanishes only because of the factor 2; dividing it out before reduction gives omega^{(2)} (and a tower omega^{(2^j)}) which vanish on the solution space but are not consequences of the original ideal; (2) Schur-Macaulay matrices generalizing Macaulay matrices from Sym^d to arbitrary Schur-module shapes lambda. Conjectured Hilbert series verified experimentally; extended to odd characteristic; breaks several MAYO/SNOVA Round-2 parameter sets.
papers.relevance: A char-2 mechanism for producing low-degree equations that are 'pseudo-solutions' (vanish on the variety, not in the ideal at that degree) is exactly the shape of lever 1's suggested proof/computation route (degree-c pseudo-solutions, closure certificates) for Weil-descended S_{m+1} over F_2. Whether divided powers of a Z-lift of the descended system add anything below d_F is unknown. Representation-theoretic Macaulay shapes also connect to the symmetry inventory (S_m, D_4 on S_5).
papers.suggested_route: Toy (sympy/msolve over F_2, n=13..21): lift the degree-2 part of the descended S_3 (or symmetrized S_4) system to Z, compute divided squares/powers, reduce mod 2, and test whether the new equations increase the rank of the degree-<=d Macaulay block below the measured last fall degree (compare against the closure certificate). Falsifier: zero rank gain at all d < d_F on all tested n, in which case the mechanism is ideal-redundant for Weil-descent systems and the lead dies.

papers.title: Efficient Polynomial System Solving via Dixon Resultants: Applications to AO Primitives
papers.authors: Haohai Suo, Jiamin Cui
papers.date: received 2026-09-10, last revised 2026-09-21 (ASIACRYPT 2026; in window by revision)
papers.summary: Revisits the Dixon resultant for eliminating several variables at once; refined upper bounds on Dixon matrix size via lattice-path counting; complexity under several determinant models; open-source C solver DRSolve; three elimination strategies applied to Poseidon, Vision, XHash12. Finding: on well-determined random systems DRSolve is competitive with Magma/msolve and better in the low-variable/high-degree regime; Groebner preferable for overdetermined systems.
papers.relevance: Summation-polynomial decomposition instances (S_{m+1} restricted to a subspace, or prime-field S_4/S_5 in few variables of degree 2^{m-1}) are the low-variable/high-degree regime where the paper reports Dixon resultants winning. Engine change only (constant factor) unless the elimination exposes structure; the programme's root-finding lever 2 (sub-N^2 structure for S_4 membership over prime bases) is where multi-variable elimination could matter.
papers.suggested_route: Toy benchmark: S_4 and S_5 over F_p (p 20..40 bits) and descended binary S_3/S_4 at n=13..25, Dixon elimination (DRSolve) vs msolve, same instances; record solve time and whether Dixon-eliminated univariate degrees expose any structure below the generic N^2 pair-table cost for S_4 membership. Falsifier: no speed-up beyond constant factor, no degree collapse.

papers.title: Computing Asymptotic Bounds for the Automated Coppersmith Method via Linear Programming
papers.authors: Zhaopeng Ding, Zhaopeng Dai, Baofeng Wu, Yanshuo Zhang, Kejun Zhang
papers.date: received 2026-05-22, last revised 2026-09-18 (ASIACRYPT 2026; in window by revision)
papers.summary: Reformulates the computation of asymptotic bounds for the Automated Coppersmith method (Meers-Nowakowski, ASIACRYPT 2023) as a linear program, giving a provably correct, explicitly computable formula; improved asymptotic bounds for the commutative-isogeny HNP, modular-inversion HNP, elliptic-curve HNP, LCG with unknown multiplier, and the leveled isogeny problem with hints for POKE.
papers.relevance: Lever 3: a small-root method for S_5 at delta ~ 1/5 against the Jochemsz-May reach 1/80. Automated shift-polynomial selection with LP-computed asymptotic delta has not been applied to the (D_4-symmetrised) S_5 lattice; the atlas entry LEAD-ICP-coppersmith-smallroot-semaev is closed_obstructed on the hand-built Jochemsz-May shape only.
papers.suggested_route: Run the Automated Coppersmith framework (Meers-Nowakowski, with the LP asymptotic bound of this paper) on S_5 and on the D_4-symmetrised S_5 at m=4 over a prime field: obtain the asymptotic delta reachable. Falsifier: delta < 0.169 (needed), which would confirm the lattice wall for every automated shift-set rather than one hand-chosen one. Pure computation, no curve data needed.

papers.title: Attacking CRT-RSA with Small Exponents via Unravelled Linearization
papers.authors: Zhaopeng Ding, Yanshuo Zhang, Zhaopeng Dai, Ziyang Yan, Ying Chen
papers.summary: Coppersmith attack on balanced CRT-RSA with small d_p, d_q via unravelled linearization: same asymptotic bound N^{0.122} as Takayasu-Lu-Peng (JoC 2019) but lattices of about half the dimension, theory matching experiments; new attacks exploiting MSB leakage of p+q and of d_p, d_q.
papers.relevance: Lattice lever 3, engineering side: unravelled linearization halves lattice dimension without changing the asymptotic bound. For Semaev-system lattices it would be a constant-factor device only (brief rule 5); recorded as a technique to combine with the automated Coppersmith run above.
papers.suggested_route: Only as an add-on to the 2026/1027 experiment: apply unravelled linearization to the S_5 lattice to see whether the practical dimension at which the asymptotic delta is approached shrinks. Classify as engineering.

papers.title: Provable Lattice Reduction in Nearly the Time of QR Factorization
papers.authors: Yang Zhou, Zhedong Wang, Mingsheng Wang
papers.summary: Deterministic, heuristic-free lattice reduction with bit complexity O~(n^omega (1 + log kappa_col(B))), matching QR factorization up to log factors (iterative precision management, finer potential analysis, new basis/transform representation). Implementation beats flatter (CRYPTO 2023) on all 153 tests including Coppersmith-type inputs (median instruction ratio 1.55 q-ary, 1.86 NTRU-like).
papers.relevance: Engineering for any lattice experiment in the programme (Semaev small-root lattices, EC-HNP). Constant factor.
papers.suggested_route: Use as the reducer in the S_5 lattice runs if dimensions exceed what fplll/flatter handle in 20 CPU-minutes. No falsifier; engineering.

papers.title: Generic Bounds for Multi-Instance Problems: The Strange Case of Inverse Diffie-Hellman
papers.authors: Akshima, Eike Kiltz, Aysan Nishaburi, Samin Nooripoor, Emiel Wiedijk
papers.summary: Generic-group hardness of multi-instance CDH, SDH, IDH, LKDH in prime-order groups: multi-instance CDH/SDH as hard as k independent DLs; multi-instance IDH/LKDH provably easier in some regimes; all keep (log p + log k)/2 bits. Technique: extends Yun's hyperplane-query model; reduces lower bounds to the 'zero-hyperplane-query' advantage and bounds it via Krull dimension of algebraic varieties computed by Groebner bases / counting algebraically independent coordinate-ring elements.
papers.relevance: The programme's Generic-oracle wall (S T^2 >= r/|Aut| for decomposition oracles with advice) is stated via Corrigan-Gibbs-Kogan; this paper supplies an algebraic-geometry toolkit (Krull dimension of the variety of the oracle's queries) that could give a tighter or more general statement for m-sum decomposition oracles, and clarifies which oracle types escape (representation-dependent ones). Closure itself already in atlas (LEAD-EXO-augmented-oracle-ggm, LEAD-ICE-generic-oracle-arity-cost-floor).
papers.suggested_route: Theory note only: write the m-sum decomposition oracle as a hyperplane-query game, compute the Krull dimension of the relation variety, and check whether the resulting generic bound reproduces or sharpens B D^2 >> N. No experiment.

papers.title: Graphs and cycles in curve-based collision walks
papers.authors: Sebastiano Boscardin, Jolijn Cottaar, Monika Trimoska
papers.summary: Multi-user collision attacks (van Oorschot-Wiener style) on ECDLP and on supersingular isogeny pathfinding over F_{p^2} and F_p. For ECDLP: all L keys recovered from L useful collisions, no infiltrator. Over F_{p^2}: about L + log L collisions, no infiltrator; over F_p: about 0.75 L keys from L collisions, infiltrator required. Proposes new pseudorandom walks suited to isogeny pathfinding.
papers.relevance: Multi-target rho / precomputation baseline for the fairness audits (equal-advice Bernstein-Lange). The ECDLP part is the known Kuhn-Struik/Fouque-Joux-Mavromati regime (LEAD-RHO-dp-multitarget-precomputation closed_known, LEAD-ICB-multi-target-and-portfolio closed_obstructed); new content is on isogeny walks. Trimoska is also the SAT-for-point-decomposition author (2019/313), but this paper has no index-calculus content.
papers.suggested_route: None for IC. Cite as the current multi-target generic reference when pricing any multi-target IC claim.

papers.title: Accelerating Pollard Rho with GPU Field Arithmetic on NVIDIA Blackwell
papers.authors: Adam Buran, Kevin Nguyen
papers.summary: Programme-authored. ECC2K-130 rho (expected 2^{60.9} iterations) on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell: packed normal-basis representation (Frobenius as permutation network), PTX clmad carry-less multiply (131-bit product in six instructions), 3-input logic, measured batch/launch geometry; 0.85 -> 14.64 G iter/s audited (17.2x; later build 15.88), about 230x the 2010 GPU kernel per card, challenge under five GPU-years; measured pipe-rate upper bound 24-26 G iter/s; P-256 1.632 and P-384 0.548 G iter/s; walk constant measured 2^{60.91}-2^{60.92}; FPGA engine 8.25 G iter/s on AWS F2; campaign walked 2^{56.68} iterations (5.4% of expected).
papers.relevance: Sets the rho reference every IC proposal must be priced against for ECC2K-130 (brief section 4). It is the programme's own work (LEAD-RHO-ecc2k130-gpu-fpga-throughput, LEAD-RHO-native-step-cost, LEAD-RHO-ecc2k130-iteration-function).
papers.suggested_route: None; use its per-iteration costs as the price band for GAE conversions in this pass.

papers.title: Scalable Small ECDLP Solver via Windowed-Batch Inversion for Additively Homomorphic Encryption
papers.authors: Murat Cenk, Muhammad ElSheikh, Irem Keskinkurt Paksoy, M. Anwar Hasan
papers.summary: Small-interval ECDLP (EC-ElGamal decryption) on secp256k1: Jacobian-coordinate giant steps, windowed batch inversion (per-thread memory O(2^{l2}) -> O(W)), co-Z arithmetic; no giant-step table (FastECDLP needed 5.91 GB at 58 bits, 378 GB at 64 bits); up to 2.3x faster than FastECDLP at 54/58 bits; 63-bit in 53 s and 64-bit in 105 s on a Core Ultra 9 285K.
papers.relevance: Interval DLP engineering (BSGS/kangaroo family), closed_known / closed_dominated in the atlas (LEAD-RHO-bsgs-family-memory, LEAD-RHO-kangaroo-interval). Only useful as a step-cost datapoint for batched-inversion rho on prime curves (LEAD-RHO-batched-inversion-shared-pm closed_known).
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Faster complete formulas and their application to curves with efficient endomorphisms
papers.authors: Diego F. Aranha, Paulo L. Barreto
papers.summary: For y^2 = x^3 + b, p = 1 mod 3 (secp256k1, BN, BLS): complete addition improved from 12M to 11M (10M mixed) via a 3D cross-product final stage; complete tripling at the cost of incomplete Jacobian tripling; exception-free width-3 tau-NAF with tau = 1 - omega and a six-point table, about 14% faster than exception-free GLV at 256 bits; RELIC and libsecp256k1 (+5.2% fixed-base) implementations; 'imaginary' Toom-Cook for G_T.
papers.relevance: Step-cost engineering for rho on j=0 prime curves (LEAD-RHO-cheaper-step-primitives open_unexamined; LEAD-RHO-native-step-cost). Also relevant to the programme's own P-256 rho numbers in 2026/2469. Constant factor. Related: 2024/1906 (Xu-Yu-Han-Lu, revised 2026-09-30) on efficient arithmetic for the same family.
papers.suggested_route: Engineering: fold the 11M/10M complete addition (and the tau=1-omega structure for j=0 curves) into the rho step-cost model for secp256k1-type curves; no falsifier.

papers.title: Detecting split surfaces, RM surfaces, and minimum walks on isogeny graphs
papers.authors: Eda Kirimli, Gaurish Korpal
papers.summary: Detects (N,N)-splittings of principally polarized superspecial abelian surfaces and computes the minimum (N,N)-splitting level of a superspecial Jacobian without constructing isogeny paths, by replacing isogeny computations with primitive-representation problems for positive definite quadratic forms in five variables (refined Humbert invariants); same framework detects embeddings of real-multiplication orders. Experiments: 11 <= p <= 251 exhaustive (matches Ibukiyama-Katsura-Oort counts) and up to 1000-bit p (splitting degrees with log2 N ~ log2 p, i.e. (N,N)-isogeny of degree ~ p^2).
papers.relevance: Lever 10 of the brief (Prym / same-field genus-g embeddings of E in a Jacobian; second N-torsion direction via Kani/Richelot gluing; five filed follow-ups unexecuted). Supplies a way to find split Jacobians J ~ E x E' and the splitting level via quadratic forms rather than isogeny search. Setting is superspecial (char p, supersingular), not ordinary curves; the atlas leads LEAD-TRF-same-field-genus-g-embedding and LEAD-EXO-split-jacobian-projection are closed_obstructed, so this is a tool for a closed mechanism unless the Prym follow-ups reopen it.
papers.suggested_route: Only if the Prym/Kani follow-ups are executed: use refined Humbert invariants to enumerate (N,N)-split genus-2 Jacobians containing a given toy E over the same field and record whether any N-torsion direction gives a relation source the transport-conservation lemma does not cover. Falsifier: decomposition counts obey |kernel|^{m-1} exactly.

papers.title: Cyclic isogeny walks on genus-zero modular curves
papers.authors: Aleksei Udovenko
papers.summary: Organizes the algebraic maps for genus-zero X_0(N) (single-parameter models: Montgomery, Edwards, Jacobi quartic, Hessian, Deuring normal form, related by degree-1 maps), gives rational lifts from the j-line to X_0(N), and defines/computes non-backtracking modular polynomials via an extended Elkies method (lower degree, sparser, smoother walk models, carry an auxiliary isogeny); radical representations of the same relation; application to compact R1CS encodings of isogeny proofs.
papers.relevance: Curve-presentation question (LEAD-ICE-curve-presentation-invariance open_next_step; LEAD-EXO-curve-model-representation closed_obstructed): the programme found first fall degree is a constant of the presentation and d_F presentation-dependent. X_0(N)-parametrised single-parameter models are a systematic family of presentations on which summation polynomials could be re-derived. Isogeny-walk content itself is covered by transport conservation / Tate (closed).
papers.suggested_route: Low priority toy: derive S_3 on Montgomery/Edwards/Hessian/Deuring models for one binary and one prime toy curve and check whether d_ff or the measured D of the descended system changes with the model (prediction from the programme: d_ff constant, D possibly presentation-dependent). Falsifier for the lead: identical D across models.

papers.title: Getting to the right root: radical isogenies of every degree (and 2026/2661: Radical isogenies on every model)
papers.authors: Thomas Decru
papers.summary: 2595: proves corrected linear-size radical isogeny formulae for every N >= 4 over any field of characteristic coprime to 2N; every building block is a twisted sum of a discrete Kronecker function over Z/NZ and the formulae follow from a distribution relation for the Kronecker theta function. 2661: radical N-isogeny steps of every odd degree directly on short Weierstrass, Montgomery, twisted Edwards, Huff, Jacobi quartic, twisted Hessian, Legendre, Jacobi intersection, Kummer lines, with exact inversion-free operation counts (10N multiplications per step in Tate normal form, etc.).
papers.relevance: Isogeny chains as relation transport are closed by the transport-conservation lemma (kernel symmetry only, trivial at prime order). The Kronecker theta / distribution-relation machinery is adjacent to the closed elliptic-net lead (LEAD-EXO-elliptic-net-eds, GGM-simulable). Recorded as a 'random idea' connector only.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: When Elliptic-Curve Semiprimality Certificates Reveal Factors
papers.authors: Giuseppe Vitto
papers.summary: Formalizes Goldwasser-Kilian-style semiprimality certificates (N, S, E, P) with a prime point order S > (N^{1/6}+1)^2. For CM-constructed certificates, a norm-lattice reconstruction factors N from (N, S, D) alone in expected polynomial time when Frobenius at every prime divisor lies in a known imaginary quadratic field of discriminant D (or has trace zero) and gcd(S, 2DN) = 1; plus public-point and quadratic-twist attacks; factors Reble's 1084-digit and Broadhurst's 5061-digit moduli.
papers.relevance: CM Frobenius data plus a small lattice leaks factors of N; for ECDLP over a prime field the Frobenius of a CM curve (secp256k1, j=0) is already public and the atlas has LEAD-STR-secp256k1-cm-class-audit and LEAD-STR-small-cm-disc-nonunit-endo closed_obstructed. No ECDLP route; recorded as 'lattices for small roots / EC' adjacent.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Forging 1024-bit RSA signatures in nearly SNFS time
papers.authors: Laura Shea, Miro Haller, Adam Suhl, Nadia Heninger, Emmanuel Thome
papers.summary: Implements the 2007 Joux-Naccache-Thome oracle-assisted algorithm: with 2^32 raw RSA signing-oracle queries (an HSM), forges 1024-bit RSA signatures in about SNFS time without factoring: 1380 core-years over five months (mostly precomputation), then any forgery offline in 180 core-years. Extrapolation: 15-30 bits below factoring-based estimates for 1024-4096-bit RSA. Companion: 2026/2256 (Buzatoiu-Maimut-Naccache, revised 2026-10-23) gives the Rabin (e=2) case in L_n(1/3, (32/9)^{1/3}).
papers.relevance: Finite-field/NFS-adjacent record and the oracle-assisted paradigm, whose elliptic analogue is Joux-Vitse oracle-assisted static DH on E(F_{q^n}) (FRONTIER known_bound) and Cheon/Brown-Gallant on prime curves (LEAD-RHO-cheon-* leads). Recorded per task instruction (finite-field DLP / algebraic records); no new ECDLP mechanism.
papers.suggested_route: None for IC; cite as the current oracle-assisted algebraic record when discussing LEAD-ICP-gfp5-oa-sdhp-jv.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Open-Source Groebner Basis Implementations for Small-Scale AES Polynomial Systems over GF(2)
papers.authors: Pavel Holy, Martin Jurecek
papers.summary: 20 open-source Groebner implementations vs Magma on small-scale AES systems over GF(2) with field equations. On the Hard set only msolve and Singular slimgb finished all runs (164 s / 3693 MiB and 269 s / 4343 MiB vs Magma 319 s / 16853 MiB); msolve used 13.4 cores on average, fastest in Easy and Hard; Magma fastest in Medium.
papers.relevance: Confirms msolve (the programme's engine) as the best open-source choice over GF(2) for the descended systems; LEAD-ICE-boolean-f4-f5-f6-engines is closed_dominated. Engineering datapoint only.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Refined Application of the XL Algorithm within the Algebraic Approach to the Regular Syndrome Decoding Problem
papers.authors: Hiroki Furue, Yusuke Aikawa
papers.summary: Algebraic RSDP solvers following the Wang et al. hybrid framework but allowing arbitrary XL solving degree d; XFL variant (partial Gaussian elimination + guessing) and WXL variant (sparse Macaulay matrix, Wiedemann). WXL with d > 2 wins for small block size beta; hybrid wins as beta grows. (Related: 2026/2563-2564 'Regular Syndrome Decoding Is Easier Than Previously Estimated', withdrawn 2026-10-22.)
papers.relevance: Hybrid guess-and-determine plus XL at chosen solving degree is the same design space as LEAD-ICE-hybrid-guess-determine-l7 (open_next_step) for the descended S_{m+1}: trade guessed variables for solving degree. Engineering/accounting.
papers.suggested_route: Reuse their cost model shape (guess k variables, solve at degree d with sparse Wiedemann) to re-price the hybrid lead on binary S_3/S_4 cells; no new falsifier.

papers.title: Low-Space Quantum Discrete Logarithms on Genus-Two Jacobians
papers.authors: Yan Huang, Yuling Chen, Fangguo Zhang
papers.summary: Randomized reduction making generic divisor-addition formulas usable in quantum phase computation despite exceptional inputs (two independent public group seeds, odd order); applied to odd prime-order subgroups of genus-2 Jacobians over F_q (monic quintic, zero quartic coefficient) with integer-lift Mumford arithmetic, a terminal polynomial and a shifted Legendre symbol; 10n + o(n) logical qubits; Gaudry-Schost instance over F_{2^127-1}: 1923 qubits (16-bit window, Toffoli < 2^60) or 1618 qubits (32-bit window, ~2^70.43 Toffoli). Companion in window: 2026/2665 (Pappalardo et al., cat qubits): secp256k1 ECDLP at most 30,000 cat qubits and 1 hour under stated noise assumptions; FFDLP-512 about 6,700 cat qubits and 21 minutes.
papers.relevance: Quantum resource estimates; outside the classical index-calculus scope. Atlas: LEAD-EXO-quantum-ecdlp-resources open_next_step. Recorded for completeness.
papers.suggested_route: None in this pass.

papers.title: Smoothness of Shortest Isogenies to Frobenius Conjugates (with 2026/1821 and 2026/2530)
papers.authors: Yi Ouyang, Wei Wei, Zheng Xu (2677); Maher Mamah (1821); Marc Houben, Lam L. Pham (2530)
papers.summary: 2677 bounds the smoothness probability of the minimal degree delta_E of an isogeny E -> E^{(p)} for random supersingular E, making Wesolowski's p^{1/3+o(1)} endomorphism-ring algorithm (2026/1486) unconditional, plus a uniform asymptotic formula (Dirichlet L-values) for existence of a degree-n connecting isogeny. 1821: concrete cost and time-memory analysis of that attack (improves state of the art only at NIST Level I over practical memory; vOW variant recovers it with parallelism; quantum claw-finding variants; SageMath implementation). 2530: non-scalar polarized endomorphism of a superspecial PPAS in p^{4/5+o(1)} time and memory.
papers.relevance: The structural lesson of the supersingular p^{1/3} line is that Frobenius-conjugate shortcuts in the isogeny graph beat generic collision search; for ordinary curves over F_p or F_{2^n} the analogous moves are covered by Tate's theorem and the transport-conservation lemma (LEAD-STR-isogeny-walk-weak-neighbour closed_known, LEAD-STR-isogeny-transport-preprocessing closed_obstructed). No ECDLP route; recorded as the main 'isogeny' cluster of the window.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Top Gun: Degree Annihilation Attacks on Poseidon (with 2026/1692 Smart Subspace Restriction)
papers.authors: Antonio Sanso, Giuseppe Vitto (1254); Amit Singh Bhati, Sundas Tariq, Tomer Ashur (1692)
papers.date: 1254 received 2026-06-14, revised 2026-09-18; 1692 received 2026-08-15, revised 2026-10-04 (both in window by revision)
papers.summary: 1254: 'degree annihilation' imposes algebraic constraints (found via elimination, resultants, Groebner bases) that force dominant degree terms of round polynomials to vanish, yielding systems of much lower effective degree; new CICO-2 attacks on reduced-round Poseidon; thesis that constructing varieties that actively control degree growth is a general direction. 1692: generalized S-box skipping via subspace restriction and (k+1)-wise collapsing, spending input degrees of freedom to linearize state transitions.
papers.relevance: Both are the 'choose a subvariety on which the degree collapses' idea; in the ECDLP setting this is exactly the factor-base-as-subspace trick (Weil descent restricted to V) and the summation-cover monodromy result says better geometry does not raise mean yield. Possible residual: constraints that annihilate the top-degree part of a descended S_{m+1} (rather than restrict to a linear subspace) have not been catalogued; LEAD-ICB-nonlinear-frob-stable-bases is open_next_step.
papers.suggested_route: Toy: for descended S_3 over F_{2^n}, n=13..21, search (Groebner/resultant) for low-degree non-linear constraint varieties on the base coordinates that annihilate the top homogeneous component of the descended system, and compare the resulting solving degree and yield against a linear subspace of the same dimension. Falsifier: no nonlinear variety beats the linear subspace at equal size (expected from the monodromy result).

papers.title: Simple Extremely Lossy Functions from Small-Exponent Hashing
papers.authors: Damiano Abram, Agni Datta, Archisman Dutta, Lawrence Roy
papers.summary: Introduces Extremely Lossy Trapdoor Hashing (implies all known ELF variants), built in one step from exponential hardness of small-exponent discrete log plus polynomial DCR; argues exponential security is needed only in the exponent size, so the assumption is plausible modulo N^2 despite subexponential index calculus in those groups.
papers.relevance: Tangential. Illustrates the accounting point that index calculus lowers the cost per group, not per exponent size, so interval/small-exponent DL stays at sqrt(interval) even where index calculus exists; the only paper in the window mentioning 'index calculus' in its abstract.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Properties of the Me Operation and Me-Scalar Multiplication on Elliptic Curves over Finite Fields
papers.authors: Masaaki Shirase
papers.summary: Studies the Me operation (elliptic-curve analogue of Yura's M operation from the box-ball system), idempotent and non-associative over finite fields; defines two Me-scalar multiplications with an auxiliary point Z (commutative; multiplicative), states that the Me versions of ECDLP are hard while the Me versions of CDH are easy, and that the second Me-scalar sequence is nonperiodic unless constant.
papers.relevance: Matched the ECDLP search only; a non-associative operation with no index-calculus content and no relation to summation polynomials. Recorded so it is not re-surfaced.
